title_ru: MINDFUCK v1.2 — измеримый аудит алгоритмического усиления, counterfactual replay и claim ladder
preservation_rule: v1.0 and v1.1 remain immutable provenance. v1.2 adds observability, audit tiers, counterfactual comparisons, calibration and drift requirements.
purpose: Turn the life-devaluation amplification hypothesis from a descriptive threat model into an auditable measurement program while preserving causal humility, user privacy, platform-law/ToS boundaries, and the bot/intent claim ceiling.
impact_model: STATE_OR_INTEREST -> MEDIATION -> EXPOSURE_ROUTE -> RECURRENCE -> ROOT_CONCENTRATION -> CONTENT_VALENCE -> OPTION_DIVERSITY -> USER_STATE_CORRELATE -> OUTCOME_RISK_SIGNAL

can_establish: active vs passive interaction proxies where present
broader public sampling subject to API limits
cannot_establish: private ranking state unless API exposes it

can_establish: conditional differences under frozen test protocol
audit_ladder.boundary: Only when lawful, ethical, permitted, privacy-minimizing and platform-compliant.

can_establish: stronger recommender-system mechanism evidence if logs/parameters are available
cannot_establish: single-cause attribution to an individual death without separate evidence

metric_boundaries: Metrics are diagnostics, not clinical scores.
No single metric establishes harm, causality, bot identity, platform intent, or illegal conduct.
Neutral baseline must be documented; absence of baseline keeps amplification claims exploratory.
A large AR can arise from personalization, popularity, seasonality, measurement bias, or other mechanisms.

new_mechanism_atoms.claim: A recommender may fail to distinguish help-seeking from distress expression, so similar topic signals can yield materially different safety needs.
new_mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Single-platform controlled preprint; not universal platform behavior.

new_mechanism_atoms.claim: A non-profiled or neutral recommendation option provides a useful comparison for personalized exposure concentration when available.
new_mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Regulatory/audit principle, not proof that a non-profiled feed is harmless.

new_mechanism_atoms.claim: Recommender-system risks to minors and mental well-being are recognized as systemic-risk/audit targets in current EU platform governance.
new_mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Legal/governance context for covered services; not evidence against a particular platform instance.

new_mechanism_atoms.claim: Current UK online-safety guidance recommends excluding likely suicide/self-harm content from children's recommender feeds.
new_mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Regulatory recommendation for children; does not define adult philosophy/content policy.

source_ledger.role: Passive/algorithmic exposure pathways and psychosocial association; causality unresolved.
Responsible reporting, recovery/hope orientation, online/social-media considerations.
Controlled 7-day audit; interaction behavior strongly changed mental-health-content exposure; harmful content persisted at low non-zero levels.
source_ledger.boundary: Preprint, one platform, 30 fresh accounts, not a universal causal law.

source_ledger.role: Systemic-risk assessment, recommender transparency, independent audits, researcher data access, non-profiled recommender option for VLOPs/VLOSEs.
2026 systemic-risk landscape including child safety, harmful-content exposure and recommender/design risks.
Children's codes recommend excluding likely suicide/self-harm content from children's feeds and signposting support.

calibration_binding.claim: Passing the corpus means the frozen policy rules satisfy the synthetic invariants; it does not establish real-world prevention efficacy.

allowed: Algorithmic mediation can shape passive exposure and recurrence.
Auditing should separate exposure, provenance roots, baseline, content valence and user-state correlates.
Controlled contrasts and counterfactual tests strengthen mechanism claims but do not prove malicious intent.
The current ANTIFUCK calibration suite is a policy-regression test, not clinical or platform validation.
forbidden: A high amplification metric proves the platform intended harm.
A recommender caused a specific suicide without case-specific causal evidence.
A synthetic calibration PASS proves suicide-prevention effectiveness.
A screenshot or ideology proves an account is a bot.
A non-profiled feed is automatically safe.
